description: Not affiliated with the U.S. government, GSA, or SAM.gov. Not a U.S. government service. Checks one federal notice against criteria YOU write. You supply the rules, for example 'Set-aside is SDVOSB' or 'Work is in Texas'; the tool marks each rule with a green check when the notice's stated field satisfies it, or no check when it does not. Every mark is labeled as a notice fact ('Notice states set-aside: ...') next to your rule text. This tool never scores, ranks, or counts: no 0-100, no percent, no 'all passed'. It does not determine eligibility, recommend bids, or suggest partners. Give the checklist any name you like, for example 'SDVOSB shop'; the name is only a label and nothing is inferred from it. Each check has three states: match (green check), no_match (the notice states a value your filter does not satisfy), or not_stated (the notice does not state the field, so your filter could not be evaluated; a blank field is never a no match). Each check shows the notice's raw stated value, and the result carries the notice's posted and retrieval dates. Every check is phrased 'The notice states X, which matches your filter Y' — never eligibility language. Follow-ups within 30 minutes after a search ride free (up to 30 per search); otherwise one accepted call counts as one use, regardless of how many criteria you check. Every result carries the standing line that a green check is a notice-field match, not a certification, size, or award determination.

notice_fact.description: What the notice states, e.g. 'Notice states set-aside: SDVOSB Set-Aside', or 'Notice states set-aside: not stated'.
notice_fact.title: Notice Fact

phrasing.description: Model-facing sentence, always in the form 'The notice states X, which matches your filter Y' (or the no-match / not-stated variant). Never eligibility language.

state.title: State

stated_value.description: The notice's raw value for this field, or null when the notice does not state it.
stated_value.title: Stated Value

empty_reason.description: 'not_loaded' (never ingested — not evidence of anything), 'no_match' (ingested, no rows match), or 'thin' (ingested, few rows)

remaining uses, and reset time. kind is 'pseudonymous' (subject hash or
